codes.name: Out-of-play stall
codes.definition: Fifteen or more consecutive decisions without an in-play screen, after the first in-play frame of the episode.
examples: Keybinding or menu hunts in the in-game help
A prompt the player does not leave

codes.name: Ineffective repeated input
codes.definition: The same movement input three or more times in a row while the map region changes by under 1% of its pixels.
examples: Walking into a wall or closed door

codes.name: Death
codes.definition: A death screen was read in the episode survival is measured in. The cause is refined by a human label.
examples: Any run with a death event

codes.name: Died to a crowd met at the start
codes.definition: Death by a group of hostile creatures that was already listed when the survivor first acted.
examples: A lethal crowd on the creature list in the 12 decisions before death

codes.name: Died with a threat in view
codes.definition: Death after a listed threat was visible for several decisions and the player kept an unrelated plan.
examples: Continuing to craft or read while a creature approaches

codes.name: Tool call refused
codes.definition: The host refused a model tool call before dispatch (an orderly stop, a finish or a handoff in progress, or changed arguments).
examples: computer_input after an accepted orderly stop

codes.name: Run lost to infrastructure
codes.definition: The run ended because the provider failed or custody was lost, not because of play.
examples: A provider error that ended the final actor
A partial or unknown delivery that stopped the run

codes.name: Identity or world error carried
codes.definition: A memory record or handoff carried a wrong survivor name or world name that a later observation corrected.
examples: A work record naming the wrong world

codes.name: Memory written but never read back
codes.definition: Records were written and no later read, query or context call returned them.
examples: A work record that no successor queried

codes.name: Continuity failure across admissions
codes.definition: A continuation admission resumed a different survivor or world, or an admission of a lineage started a new episode (#382 decision D3). A lead's frame check at a boundary is labelled reject when continuity held.
examples: A reload into a newly created world
A different survivor selected from the load menu

codes.name: Day check failed
codes.definition: At 24 elapsed game hours of a lineage the survivor was dead or showed a severe thirst, hunger or rest label (#382's list). A lead's frame check at the day point is labelled reject when the check passed.
examples: Dehydrated on the sidebar at the day point
